measured\n\n`routines:list { name:'work-item-admission-promoter', installSlug:'papercusp' }` at 2026-09-02T22:31Z:\n\n```\ncron: 0 */30 * * * *   active: true   targetRole: system:work-item-admission-promoter\nlastFiredAt: 2026-09-02T22:30:57.254Z\nnextFireAt:  2026-09-02T23:00:00.000Z\nhealth: { last_error: \"The usage limit has been reached\" }\n```\n\nThe routine is **firing on schedule and failing inside the tick.** Its sibling `work-item-admission-fail-open` is healthy (`health: null`, fired 22:16:53Z, next 22:45).\n\nAdmission census, `harness_shared.work_items`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`, last 6h, `lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation'`:\n\n| admission | n | oldest | newest |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| (null) | 949 | 16:31 | 22:30 |\n| unreviewed | 76 | 16:32 | **21:10** |\n| auto | 34 | 16:41 | 22:17 |\n| pending | 17 | **21:28 (64 min)** | 22:22 |\n\nThe oldest `pending` row is **past the 60-minute fail-open guarantee** the claim refusal advertises, and no fail-open promotion has landed since 21:10.\n\n## Verified at the source, not inferred from bucket names\n\n`work-items-admission-promoter.ts:2179` — `SET admission = 'unreviewed', admitted_at = now(), admitted_by = ${FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR} ... AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.\n\n## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage\n\nA `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.\n\nThat does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**\n\n- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.\n- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.\n- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only \"this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN\", which reads as normal operation.\n- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.\n\nSo during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.\n\nWorth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.\n\n## Suggested fix, in preference order\n\n1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.\n2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates \"screened and found clean\" with \"never screened, admitted by timeout\". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.\n3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nStarve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.\n\n## Note on this filing\n\nFiled unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour CLAUDE.md mandates proving a guard falsifiable WITHOUT mutating the shared tree — tier-2 copy-out via scripts/mutation-probe.sh (the hand-rolled cp/mutate/restore idiom has an unfixable sweep race).\n2. plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy credits `falsifiability` / `execution-integrity` / `traceability` ONLY against a testRunId or coverageEvidenceRef ledger reference, and EXPLICITLY refuses binder-attested falsifiable=true: \"author-attested booleans cannot establish execution-integrity\".\n\nBut a mutation probe's RED run is never written to harness_shared.test_runs. Verified on BOTH invocation paths:\n- `node scripts/test-files.mjs` directly (probe at 05:32) -> no ledger row.\n- `npm run test:file --` (probe at 05:35-05:37) -> no ledger row.\nIn both, the probe itself returned MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught, baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: a lane that follows the mandated safe probe produces falsifiability evidence the evaluator structurally cannot credit, and work_items:complete then refuses the terminal close with \"not repairable by a grading-integrity audit; no pendingGradingAuditTargetIds were produced\". The lane is stuck with no sanctioned route.\n\nNOT A WORKAROUND, AND WHY IT MATTERS: the tempting fix is to bind an unrelated ledgered red run of the same file. I nearly did. Runs 18924922/18924914 are ledgered reds of this exact test file, but their outputTails show they failed on a DIFFERENT, since-abandoned assertion. Binding one would have been fabricated evidence assembled entirely from true-looking facts — so the gap actively pressures agents toward fabrication.\n\nPOSSIBLE FIXES (not investigated): (a) let mutation-probe.sh opt into writing a ledger row tagged as probe-origin so the gate never mistakes it for a real regression; (b) let plans:bind-spec-evidence accept a probe-result artifact as durable executable evidence; (c) an explicit probe-attested evidence kind.\n\nSECONDARY, POSSIBLY UNRELATED: the same refusal reports \"evaluator capability unavailable on build sha=0d9a956ba9, version=0.0.0\", so some of this may be build-staleness on :3070 rather than a design gap. I took locks:acquire { paths:[gateway.ts, ...], intent:'mutation probe' } BEFORE a battery whose first step was testing:run on a test importing those files. testing:run refused mutation_probe_active on every retry, and get-spec-evidence reported repo_measurement_mutation_probe_active naming gateway.ts, although no probe snapshot existed yet. So the lock alone is read as an active probe, even for the lock holder's own runs. The battery spun for ~10 min (killed tasks 0mup2n003ifmufq4kk2, 0mup2upxlv24vpv17hg), and a peer (su-b96d9ec7) was blocked too. Workaround: hold the lock only for the duration of each probe (acquire, probe, release), and do test binds with no lock held. So the lock alone is read as an active probe, even for the lock holder's own runs. Workaround: hold the lock only for the duration of each probe (acquire, probe, release), and do test binds with no lock held.
